task: Dispatched two independent Fable (frontier-tier) reviews: (1) scrutinized the concurrency-bug investigation and stderr-write fix from the prior queue entry, (2) assessed whether docs/code-map/map.json (and the map-code skill itself) would have surfaced this bug faster. Fable identified the precise mechanism (a merged/corrupted stderr line whose sequential-if marker parsing accepts a foreign sid, poisoning sticky active_seg_id state) and two additional real gaps: (a) the log_listener's permit-by-default filter for lines with no extractable task_id, (b) a WarmWorker stale-stderr-queue leak across reused workers. Implemented defense-in-depth fixes for both, discovered and fixed a SECOND independent unlocked-stderr-write site (diagnostics.py's emit_diagnostics) via the new checked invariant Fable recommended, and applied Fable's specific map.json content recommendations directly (not just queued).

app/orchestration/scheduler/orchestrator.summary: Added known_task_segment_ids (union of every script entry's full member-id list) and a foreign-sid guard in the START_SEGMENT marker handler: a real marker naming a sid not in this dispatch's own script is ignored (WARN-logged) rather than adopted as active_seg_id -- scoped to context.ephemeral (fan-out children only; the older marker-driven multi-group SynthesisTask path legitimately discovers later groups' ids via markers, so its script may not fully enumerate every id up front).

app/engines/watchdog.py.summary: Added _KNOWN_MARKER_TOKENS and a merged-line tripwire in _drain_stream: any physical line embedding more than one marker token logs a WARNING (diagnostic only, does not drop/alter dispatch) -- the read-side signal for the write-side race fixed in engine.py/diagnostics.py.

plugins/tts_xtts/plugin/core/warm_worker.summary: WarmWorker.run_job now discards any stale _stderr_q entries before writing a new job to stdin -- closes a second, independent cross-attribution channel: _relay_trailing_stderr's fixed 0.3s grace window can leave a prior job's trailing marker line queued when the worker is reused for a new job, which would otherwise get relay_marker-stamped with the NEW job's task_id.

plugins/tts_xtts/plugin/core/diagnostics.summary: Moved the stderr write lock here (STDERR_WRITE_LOCK, emit_stderr_atomic) from server/engine.py -- discovered via dry-running the new checked invariant that emit_diagnostics() had its OWN unlocked sys.stderr.write()/flush(), a second independent instance of the exact same race (called extensively from implementation.py's xtts_generate/xtts_generate_script, per-HTTP-request on the server threadpool). engine.py now imports and reuses this SAME lock instance instead of defining a separate one -- a separate lock per writer would not have serialized the two writers against each other.

plugins/tts_xtts/plugin/server/engine.py.summary: _emit_stderr_atomic is now a thin wrapper delegating to diagnostics.py's shared emit_stderr_atomic/STDERR_WRITE_LOCK (removed the module's own separate lock).

tests/orchestration/test_dispatch_isolat.summary: Added ephemeral param to _make_task; added test_start_segment_with_foreign_sid_is_ignored and test_start_segment_with_own_group_member_sid_is_accepted (R1 revert-checked).

tests/orchestration/test_watchdog_progre.summary: Added test_merged_marker_line_logs_a_warning and test_clean_single_marker_line_does_not_warn for the tripwire.

plugins/tts_xtts/tests/test_diagnostics_.summary: New file: 3 tests for diagnostics.py's lock -- basic tee behavior, shared-lock-instance assertion (engine.py must not redefine its own), and a concurrency test proving unlocked emit_diagnostics interleaves and the fix closes it (R1 revert-checked).

docs/code-map/map.json.summary: Applied Fable's specific recommendations directly (not just queued): (1) corrected the stale app/orchestration/scheduler/resources.py file note (previously said admission is OFF by default -- now correctly says ON, with the gate/cap distinction spelled out); (2) corrected the parallel-segment-fanout flow's invariant text (previously only mentioned tts_parallel_cap, now states BOTH ENGINE_CLASS_ADMISSION and tts_parallel_cap are required); (3) added an honesty caveat to that flow's verified_by (the cited e2e test exercises the mixed-engine leg only, bypassing the exact xtts marker-relay path that broke); (4) added a new flow tts-server-marker-relay tracing the actual path that broke (orchestrator_helpers -> bridge_remote -> tts_client -> tts_server/server.py's threadpool -> engine.py/diagnostics.py -> warm_worker.py -> shared stderr -> watchdog); (5) added a new checked invariant tts-server-shared-stream-single-writer with a grep-expressible check, scoped to server-context code (explicitly excluding warm-worker-subprocess code which is single-threaded-per-process and safe by construction) -- this check is what caught the second diagnostics.py hazard; (6) added an execution-topology note to the tts_xtts module record (always-loaded at warm-start, per Fable's finding that the disambiguating gate/cap fact existed pre-incident but was filed only in an on-demand file note, never reaching the warm-start layer).

flow_impact: tts-server-marker-relay (new) and parallel-segment-fanout (corrected) both updated in the same change as the code fixes -- no drift window. meta.file_hashes/repo_checksum NOT recomputed in this pass (content-only edit to flows/invariants/notes, which are model-authored records, not source hashes) -- a future full consolidation should still recompute hashes for the source files touched (orchestrator_helpers.py, watchdog.py, warm_worker.py, diagnostics.py, engine.py) and drain this queue plus the two prior pending entries (20260706T155705Z, 20260706T184446Z).
